why_this_file: THE ONE LIST of this repository's gate legs. It used to be two: this file declared 7 legs and scripts/battery.sh ran 23, neither a superset of the other — battery.sh never ran estate-guard, and this file declared none of the posture, console, Gleam, Python or TypeScript legs. Which gates you lost depended on which runner you used, so the answer to 'is this repo green?' depended on who asked. The cure is subtraction, not a drift-checker: a checker would be a third copy. scripts/battery.sh now executes exactly what is declared here, so the two sets cannot differ by construction. Every leg's cmd is self-contained and runnable by any runner from the repository root.

legs.name: rust:fmt
legs.cmd: cargo fmt --all -- --check
legs.why: Formatting is checked, never auto-applied, so a formatting change is a reviewed diff rather than a silent one.

legs.name: rust:clippy
legs.cmd: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
legs.why: --all-targets is load-bearing: without it tests and benches are not linted, which is where bypasses accumulate.

legs.name: rust:test
legs.cmd: . scripts/gates/lib.sh || exit $?; paired_test cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast
legs.why: --no-fail-fast cost a P0 by its absence on 2026-07-31: cargo test stops at the first failing TARGET, so one red lib test silently un-runs every integration target after it and the surviving tally still reads complete. paired_test asserts the run REACHED THE END by pairing target starts with result lines — see scripts/gates/lib.sh for why counting them does not work.

legs.name: rust:test-all-features
legs.cmd: . scripts/gates/lib.sh || exit $?; paired_test cargo test --workspace --all-features --no-fail-fast
legs.why: The all-features resolution differs from the default one — --workspace resolves some features ON that -p <crate> leaves off — so this is a genuinely different run, not a slower copy of rust:test.

legs.name: posture:worker-default
legs.cmd: . scripts/gates/lib.sh || exit $?; posture_control "aion-worker, default features" liminal_transport_absent_from_this_build liminal_transport_compiled_here cargo test -p aion-worker --lib build_coverage::
legs.why: A default-OFF feature gates an entire surface, so a per-package run compiles none of it and exits 0. The gate asserts BOTH directions — the posture-appropriate announcement appeared AND its opposite did not — because a printed announcement nothing checks is observability, not a gate.

legs.name: gates:costly-announced
legs.cmd: . scripts/gates/lib.sh || exit $?; costly_announcements
legs.why: Costly proofs announce their own absence (#86), so a proof that did not run cannot read as one that passed.

legs.name: posture:serde-json-sorted
legs.cmd: . scripts/gates/lib.sh || exit $?; posture_control "aion-package ALONE, default features" "SERDE_JSON_MAP=key_sorted" "SERDE_JSON_MAP=insertion_ordered" cargo test -p aion-package --lib build_coverage:: -- --nocapture
legs.why: serde_json/preserve_order swaps Map from a key-sorted BTreeMap to an insertion-ordered IndexMap, which changes a compiled package's bytes and therefore its content hash. NO CRATE HERE ASKS FOR IT — it arrives by cargo feature unification, so it can turn on with no diff in this repository at all. -p aion-package ALONE is load-bearing: the resolution depends on which packages are named. -- --nocapture is load-bearing: a runtime-detected announcement is printed by the running test and cargo swallows it otherwise.

legs.name: posture:serde-json-insertion
legs.cmd: . scripts/gates/lib.sh || exit $?; posture_control "aion-package, preserve_order forced ON" "SERDE_JSON_MAP=insertion_ordered" "SERDE_JSON_MAP=key_sorted" cargo test -p aion-package --features serde_json/preserve_order --lib build_coverage:: -- --nocapture
legs.why: The ON arm, pinned by name rather than left to resolution. Under OFF every *_independent_of_insertion_order test is VACUOUS — Map is a BTreeMap, so two differently-ordered fixtures are the same object and asserting they serialize alike compares a value with itself.

legs.name: rust:preserve-order-pins
legs.cmd: . scripts/gates/lib.sh || exit $?; paired_test cargo test -p aion-package -p aion-awl --features serde_json/preserve_order --no-fail-fast
legs.why: The claim itself, under the resolution where it is not vacuous: every ordering-sensitive pin in the two crates that walk Maps for structure.

legs.name: gleam:aion-flow
legs.cmd: . scripts/gates/lib.sh || exit $?; require_tool gleam "The canonical Gleam workflow API and its example consumers require compile-and-test coverage." || exit $?; in_dir gleam/aion_flow gleam test
legs.why: gleam build only compiles the src half; gleam test is required to catch stale total constructors in test support, including the AgentOutcome contract break that motivated this gate.

legs.name: gates:worker-crate
legs.cmd: . scripts/gates/lib.sh || exit $?; in_dir workflows/gates/worker bash -c 'first=0; cargo fmt --check; s=$?; [ "$first" -eq 0 ] && first=$s; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings; s=$?; [ "$first" -eq 0 ] && first=$s; cargo test; s=$?; [ "$first" -eq 0 ] && first=$s; exit "$first"'
legs.why: workflows/gates/worker is deliberately its OWN cargo workspace, so every workspace-wide Rust gate compiles NONE of it — and it is the crate that RUNS the workflow battery. An instrument nothing gates is how a mutation to a gate command ships silently. The three checks do NOT short-circuit: &&-chaining would hide the clippy and test answers behind a formatting failure. The exit code is the FIRST failure's, so the verdict is unchanged and only the diagnosis is complete.

legs.name: python:aion-worker
legs.cmd: . scripts/gates/lib.sh || exit $?; require_tool uv "The Python SDKs and their proto-drift gates are uv projects." || exit $?; in_dir sdks/python/aion-worker uv run --extra dev python -m pytest tests/ -q
legs.why: These carry the proto-drift gates that are the remediation for the wire-dead SDK incident. cargo test does not run them; nothing did until the house battery existed.

legs.why: 🔴 These three were previously guarded by a bare `command -v bun`, which SILENTLY SKIPPED them when bun was absent — in direct contradiction of the battery's own stated law that a missing toolchain is a failure, not a skip, and for the very proto-drift gates that law was written about. They now refuse with 127 like every other leg.

legs.name: estate-guard
legs.cmd: [ -n "${ABLATIVE_ESTATE_ROOT:-}" ] || { printf "REFUSED rc3: estate-guard requires ABLATIVE_ESTATE_ROOT, declared in this leg .environment. It is unset at this venue, so the estate claim census is UNMEASURED here — report it as a named declared omission, never a pass.\n" >&2; exit 3; }; sh "$ABLATIVE_ESTATE_ROOT/tools/gates/hooks/check_must_be_claimed.sh" "$ABLATIVE_ESTATE_ROOT"
legs.why: This leg asserts an ESTATE property, so it needs the estate root — which is not derivable from this repository. It was previously two hardcoded absolute Mac paths, which made the leg pass only on one machine and fail opaquely everywhere else. Declaring the requirement makes an off-estate venue REFUSE with rc 3 naming the missing declaration, so the run routes to a NAMED DECLARED OMISSION rather than a silent skip or a false green.
